title: Defer off-screen content in scrollable screens
goal: Reduce initial layout and rendering work on long native screens by lazily constructing off-screen sections while preserving the non-scrollable Chat layout.
context: ScreenScaffold currently wraps all scrollable screen sections in a regular VStack inside a ScrollView. Screens such as Settings contain many panels and controls, so this eagerly builds the entire content tree before the user scrolls. Use LazyVStack only when scrollable is true; keep the existing VStack for scrollable=false to avoid changing fixed Chat layout behavior.
forbidden_changes: Do not change screen content, order, spacing, navigation, or control behavior.
Do not apply lazy layout to scrollable=false screens.
Do not modify Chat stream/runtime/provider behavior, Orb, or startup error handling.
Do not claim measured device performance improvement without physical-device measurements.
acceptance_criteria: Scrollable ScreenScaffold content uses LazyVStack for deferred off-screen rendering.
Non-scrollable ScreenScaffold content retains the existing VStack layout behavior.
Existing padding, spacing, alignment, screen header, and content order remain unchanged.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
Physical-device performance is reported as unmeasured unless actual iPhone evidence is collected.
verification: Review the conditional lazy/non-lazy layout branch and unchanged modifiers.
Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: Revert the single task commit if native build fails or scrolling/layout regressions are reported.
